verses.1: And when he gathered those twelve together, he gave them power and authority over all demons and diseases, so that they could heal them.
verses.2: And he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
verses.3: And he said to them, “Do not take anything with you on this journey: neither wood, nor bread, nor silver, nor even two coats of clothes.”
verses.4: And wherever you enter a house, there you will remain, and from there you will also leave.
verses.5: And those who refuse to accept you, you should throw away their coins from their feet as a symbol of their rejection.
verses.6: And they went out, preaching the good news and healing people everywhere.
verses.7: Herodes, the tetrarch, heard all that was happening. He also learned from those who said that John had risen from the dead.
verses.8: Some believed that Elyas appeared as a prophet, while others believed that he was one of the ancient prophets.
verses.9: Herod said, “I have killed John the Baptist.” Who is this person about whom I hear such things? He wanted to see him himself.
verses.10: And when the apostles recounted to him all they had done, he forgave them and took them to a city called Bethsaida.
verses.11: And the crowd, knowing this, followed him. And after greeting them, he spoke to them about the kingdom of God. He also gave them advice on how to manage their affairs.
verses.12: And that day began to wind down. When the twelve men came forward, they said to him, “Please calm the crowd down. Let us go and inspect the villages and farms to find out if there is any rebellion. For he is still in a remote place in the desert.”
verses.13: He said to them, “Give us something to eat.” But they replied, “We don’t have anything more than five loaves of bread and two fish. If we go to the market, we can get enough food for the whole crowd.”
verses.14: For they were indeed men who numbered fifty. He said to his disciples, “Punish them with a punishment that is proportional to their number—that is, fifty times as severe.”
verses.15: And they did so, and they eliminated everyone.
verses.16: After taking the five kinds of bread and the two kinds of fish, he looked up to heaven, praised them, and commanded that they be offered to the congregation.
verses.17: And we all ate and were satisfied. Then, twelve men brought them more food.
verses.18: And while he was praying for himself, the disciples gathered around him. He asked them, “What do the people say about me?”
verses.19: Those who answered said, “John the Baptist.” Others said, “Elias.” Still others said that it was some ancient prophet who was raised from the dead.
verses.20: He said to them, “What do you call me?” Peter replied, “The Son of God.”
verses.21: But he scolded them, telling them not to say such things.
verses.22: I said that the son of a man must suffer many hardships and be despised by the elders, high priests, and officials. He must also rise up on the third day.
verses.23: He said to everyone, “If anyone wants to return to me, I will refuse myself and also despise his cross every day. Then he may follow me.”
verses.24: For those who wish to save their own souls, they will surely do so. But those who try to destroy their own souls for my sake, they will indeed be able to save them.
verses.25: For what good does it do a person to gain the whole world, if they also lose themselves and suffer punishment?
verses.26: For whoever can deceive me and our words, that same son of man will also be deceived, when he comes in his glory, along with his father and the holy angels.
verses.27: I truly say to you, there are some of those who live among them who will not experience death until they see God’s kingdom.
verses.28: After these words, eight days passed. Then, after meeting with Peter, John, and James, he went up the mountain to give his teachings.
verses.29: And during his prayer, the appearance of his face changed; his hair became white and disappeared.
verses.30: And I saw two men coming up to him. They were Moses and Eleazar.
verses.31: Those who saw this in glory said that his departure was necessary so that he could serve in Jerusalem.
verses.32: But Peter and those who were with him were asleep. When they woke up, they saw his glory, as well as the two men who were with him.
verses.33: And while they were being separated from each other, Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three scenes: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He didn’t know what he was saying.
verses.34: And while he was speaking these words, clouds appeared and covered them. They were afraid of going into those clouds.
verses.35: And a voice came from the sky, saying: “This is my chosen son. Listen to him.”
verses.36: And it was Jesus alone who heard the voice during that event. He also remained silent and did not tell anyone anything about those days.
verses.37: On the sixth day, as they were leaving the mountain, a large crowd gathered around him.
verses.38: And now, a man from the crowd began to speak. He said, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son. He is my only child.”
verses.39: And it seems that a spirit takes hold of him. Suddenly, he starts to scream loudly. The spirit spreads him everywhere with its power, and then it immediately leaves him.
verses.40: And I asked your students to help me with this, but they were unable to do so.
verses.41: Then Jesus replied, “Oh, wicked and perverse generation! How long will I be with you, and bear witness against you? Bring your son here.”
verses.42: But as he was still approaching him, the demon attacked him and tried to harm him. But Jesus recognized the evil spirit with his power, raised the child up, and gave him back to his father.
verses.43: All of them were amazed at the greatness of God. All those who were in awe of Him said to His disciples, “What a wonderful creation!”
verses.44: Take these words to your hearts. For the son of man will be handed over to people to be killed by them.
verses.45: But those who knew the true nature of this symbol, and whose knowledge was kept secret from them so that they wouldn’t be aware of it, were also afraid to even mention it in relation to this symbol.
verses.46: Then, a discussion arose among them: who among them could be considered the greatest.
verses.47: But Jesus understood the thoughts of their hearts. He took the child and placed him beside himself.
verses.48: And he said to them, “Whoever accepts this child in my name, and whoever accepts me as his teacher, he indeed becomes great among you all. For the youngest among you is greater than everyone else.”
verses.49: After answering, John said, “Ephippus, I know that there is something in your name that can provoke demons. We will prevent him from following us.”
verses.50: And Jesus said to him, “Do not be afraid. For I am with you always.”
verses.51: And as the days of his purification passed by, he prepared himself to go to Jerusalem.
verses.52: And he sent messengers before his face. They went into the city of Samaria, in order to prepare everything for him.
verses.53: And they did not allow him to go, because his face was being taken to Jerusalem.
verses.54: Seeing this, the disciples said to James and John, “Lord, do you want us to send fire from heaven and put them there?”
verses.55: He also evaluated them as worthless.
verses.56: And they were sent to another kingdom.
verses.57: And as they walked along the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go.”
verses.58: And Jesus said to him, “The scorpions have holes in their backs, and the vultures in the sky will rest there. But the son of man will not have to bow his head.”
verses.59: He said to another person, “Follow me.” The other person replied, “Lord, please allow me to bury my father first before you go.”
verses.60: He said to him, “Anate the dead; bury your own dead. You, on the other hand, go and spread the kingdom of God.”
verses.61: Another person said, “I will follow you, my lord. First, please allow me to go and get things ready for my home.”
verses.62: And Jesus said, “No one who presses his hand against the wound can see that the kingdom of God is near.”
